RULES FOR THIS FILE, because the last one grew 67 top-level keys and 323 rows:
1. items[] is the content. Top-level keys are schema only - no narrative,
no timestamped manager_observation_* / manager_tick_* entries, no incident logs.
Three observations an hour apart on one row is the failure mode, not diligence.
2. ONE status field: `state`, from the `states` vocabulary below. There is no `status`.
3. `done` and `landed_unproven` are DIFFERENT FACTS and are never collapsed.
4. A row that is neither a plan item nor a live lane does not belong here.
A question goes to research/queue/<id>.yaml instead.
5. This file is served to the operator as the live Workflow page via
GET /api/bot/work/checklist, read from the VM's working tree. ict-git-sync
pulls main every ~5 min, so the page is as fresh as the last push TO MAIN.
cycle_intent: Make the promotion ladder mechanical and the research loop terminate in a decision. Edge is decided offline; a book only ever checks mechanics and cost.

priorities.decided: operator, AskUserQuestion popup in manager session_01KAQRJxRbRwpYTkPgBjNVyQ, 2026-09-28 ~08:55Z, verbatim answer "Prop first (Recommended)"
priorities.floor: anything broken on a live-money or prop money path jumps the queue, whatever its theme
order: 1 Prop account — roster (candidates ONLY from https://www.breakoutprop.com/symbols/), sizing, exits
5 Macro sleeve (M28 re-shape via research; M29 dormant until it reads out)
priorities.how_used: Lanes are assigned top-down; the research queue is weighted ~30/25/20/15/10 in this order; Fable goes to the highest-value research items at the manager's discretion (operator 2026-09-28: most Fable budget to high-value research, not every research task). Operator decisions surface as popups ranked by this order.

states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it
states.in_flight: a lane is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on the typed edge(s) in blocked_on
states.dropped: deliberately not doing; note says why

item_schema.id: plan item id (A1..D3) or a lane id
item_schema.title: one line
item_schema.lane: session id once dispatched, else null
item_schema.model: the model chosen for the lane, with the reason in `note`
item_schema.ceiling_usd: per-lane dollar ceiling; on breach READ what it produced, then kill or re-scope
item_schema.spend_usd: actual, filled in by the cost meter (A1)
item_schema.tier: 1 | 2 | 3 - the approval the resulting change needs
item_schema.blocked_on: typed edges [{kind, ref, what}] — kind is `work_item` or `operator_decision`, ref names the blocker, what says why. Empty list = nothing declared blocks it.
item_schema.note: what is true about this row. Not a log.
